title: Scalar-extension local models of the integral root line
statement:
For the concrete Tate sheaves [def-pur-twist-sheaves], assume the completed Z_l root module has rank one. The integral tensor has a pro-etale unit trivialization. At every positive finite level its completed scalar reduction is the prescribed finite tensor, which has a unit trivialization and is nonzero if the base is nonempty. Local constancy, constructibility and finite stalks follow separately from the generic proved finite-line theorem. No derived assertion is included.

theorem purTwistIntegralLocalModels
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    [∀ x : S, Invertible (l : S.residueField x)]
    (hL : (purTwistZlModule S l).IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank 1) :
    (∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (U : I → S.ProEt)
      (f : ∀ i, U i ⟶ ProEt.mk (𝟙 S)),
      Presieve.ofArrows U f ∈ (ProEt.precoverage S).coverings _ ∧
      ∀ i, Nonempty ((purTwistIntegralModule S l E).over (U i) ≅
        (SheafOfModules.unit
          (WeilConjectures.completedIntegralCoefficientSheafUnrestricted l E S)).over (U i))) ∧
    ∀ n : ℕ,
      Nonempty (SheafOfModules.changeOfRingsOfUniverses.{u, u + 1, u + 1, u + 1}
        (WeilConjectures.completedIntegralCommRingProjectionUnrestricted l E S n)
          (purTwistIntegralModule S l E) ≅ purTwistFiniteOne S l E n) ∧
      (∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (U : I → S.ProEt)
        (f : ∀ i, U i ⟶ ProEt.mk (𝟙 S)),
        Presieve.ofArrows U f ∈ (ProEt.precoverage S).coverings _ ∧
        ∀ i, Nonempty ((purTwistFiniteOne S l E n).over (U i) ≅
          (SheafOfModules.unit (WeilConjectures.integralCoefficientSheaf l E S n)).over (U i))) ∧
      (Nonempty S → ¬IsZero (purTwistFiniteOne S l E n))

proof.text: Use the proved scalar pushout comparison, then carry out ordinary scalar tensor and its finite local models.

The integral twist and its ordinary reductions. Put $L=M\otimes_{(\mathbf Z_\ell)_S}(\mathcal O_E)_S$. It has the $B=R\otimes_{(\mathbf Z_\ell)_S}(\mathcal O_E)_S$-module structure $(x\otimes a)(m\otimes b)=(xm)\otimes ab$. The tensor relations show this is well defined. On the cover of step 3, $M=R$, so $L=B$; restriction commutes with the tensor because both are formed from the same local tensor sections and sheafification relations on the slice. Thus $L$ is a line over the completed coefficient sheaf. Apply the quotient clause of lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence with $A=\mathcal O_E$, $I=(\varpi_E)$ (a Noetherian DVR by step 5's cited valuation theorem). It gives $B/\varpi_E^nB=(A_{E,n})_S$. For any $B$-module sheaf $H$, both $H\otimes_{(\mathcal O_E)_S}(A_{E,n})_S$ and $H\otimes_B(A_{E,n})_S$ canonically equal $H/\varpi_E^nH$: the mutually inverse maps are $h\otimes\bar a\mapsto\overline{ah}$ and $\bar h\mapsto h\otimes1$. Hence the two reductions of $L$ coincide with the stated $A_{E,n}(1)_S$, with their quotient projections and transition maps. Tensoring the local isomorphism $L=B$ with $(A_{E,n})_S$ proves rank one of each reduction.

Finite reductions have etale trivializations, not only the infinite pro-etale trivialization. For fixed $n$, choose $r$ with $er\geq n$, so $\ell^r A_{E,n}=0$. Tensor reassociation gives $A_{E,n}(1)_S=M\otimes_{(\mathbf Z_\ell)_S}(A_{E,n})_S$. Since $\ell^r$ annihilates the second factor, the maps $m\otimes a\mapsto\bar m\otimes a$ and $\bar m\otimes a\mapsto m\otimes a$ identify this with $(M/\ell^rM)\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/\ell^r)_S}(A_{E,n})_S$ (changing a lift by $\ell^rm'$ gives zero). By step 4 this is $\mu_{\ell^r,S}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/\ell^r)_S}(A_{E,n})_S$. Apply the etale trivialization in step 1 to identify it with $(A_{E,n})$ on that etale cover. Thus it is locally constant with finite stalks: lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift lifts any geometric point to one of these etale cover members, lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization identifies the corresponding slice site, and lem-weil-proetale-constant-sheaf-stalk identifies its stalk with the finite ring $A_{E,n}$, finite by lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients. The same three citations, applied to the step-1 isomorphisms $\mu_{\ell^r,S}|_{U_i}\cong(\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z)_{U_i}$ on the jointly surjective etale cover of step 1, identify every geometric stalk of $\mu_{\ell^r,S}$ with the finite ring $\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z$; this is the finite-stalk assertion of clause 1. This argument supplies etale-local finite coefficients even when $S$ itself is not quasi-compact.

Constructibility and the empty-base correction. The reduction complex has only the cohomology sheaf $A_{E,n}(1)_S$ in degree zero. Step 8 makes it locally constant with finite module stalks, so the single stratum $S$ is a finite locally closed constructible partition witnessing constructibility in def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility; its underlying whole subset is constructible even without any finiteness hypothesis on $S$: in def-weil-constructible-subset take the retrocompact opens $U=S$, $V=\varnothing$ (their intersections with each quasi-compact open are that open and the empty set). The subset $S$ is also locally closed as the intersection of the whole open and whole closed subset. It belongs to $D^b_c(S,A_{E,n})$ with support contained in $[0,0]$ by def-weil-cohomological-support. If $S$ is nonempty, choose a geometric point, lift it to an etale trivializing member using lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift, and use lem-weil-proetale-constant-sheaf-stalk to obtain the nonzero stalk $A_{E,n}$ ($1\notin(\varpi_E^n)$ in the local DVR). Thus the support is exactly $\{0\}$. If $S=\varnothing$, every site object is empty and covered by the empty family; the sheaf axiom forces the only module sheaf to be zero. The support is then empty. This explicit counterexample repairs the imported unconditional equality with $\{0\}$.
